_note: What Kiku, the old woman of the persimmon orchard in Minamino, says when the farmer talks to her (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction, gift_items her own answers to a keepsake and to dishes. The birthday lines (winter 25), the close lines from band 4 and the dear lines at band 6 once her band 6 scene is seen (heart_kiku_6), the bell lines once her band 5 scene is seen (heart_kiku_5). The twig rows (scion) take Tuesdays and Saturdays only, about 2 talks in 7, and carry only twig lines; on the other days her usual rows run as before, so her close and dear lines keep their share of those days. Our own lines.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Seventy-odd springs and these blossoms still make me hold my breath.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Lanterns are for walking old women home. That's what they're for, if you ask me.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: My persimmons hang drying under this same moon. They'll be sweet by winter.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Another year turned. I ring my little bell once for each person I miss. It takes a while now.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: My, you do like an old woman's chatter. Stay as long as you like.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Go on, dear. The day is short for the young and long for the old.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Oh, the young farmer. Tome told me about you. I'm Kiku. These persimmon trees are older than I am.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Mind you don't eat one straight off the branch in fall. Those are the bitter ones, for drying.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: I bow here every afternoon. The water spirit keeps the river kind to us. Will you bow too?

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Rain on the orchard. The trees drink and I nap. Everyone is happy.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Peel them, string them, hang them under the eaves. In a month they're sweet as honey.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Leave the last persimmon on the tree for the birds. Greedy farmers get thin harvests.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Dried persimmons with green tea by the hearth. That's what winter is for.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Nana comes to help me pick. She eats one for every three she puts in the basket.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Tome and I were girls together. She was the brave one. I was the one who got caught.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Horsetail comes up below my orchard, down by the far pine. Tome and I picked it as girls and peeled it on the porch, dear.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Mugwort grows thick along the lane in summer. Pick the soft tips, pound them into the rice, and you have kusa mochi, dear.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: The ginkgo by the water shrine drops its nuts in fall. They smell dreadful, but roasted they're a treat. The spirit doesn't mind sharing.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: In winter there's only enoki, by the pine at the bottom of the gardens. That's why we dry the persimmons in fall, dear.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Another year, and the water spirit let me keep it. I told her thank you this morning. Today I am allowed to be fussed over, dear.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: For me, on my birthday? Nobody has remembered it since... Well. Somebody has now.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Come in and sit, dear. You don't have to carry anything. Just sit. An old woman likes the sound of someone sitting.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Tome says I talk about you more than I talk about my own knees. That's saying a great deal.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: I rang the little bell twice in the lane yesterday, the plain note and the bright one. A crow stopped to listen. I took that as an answer.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: I'm counting the ones I'm glad of now, the way I used to count the ones I miss. The count is higher than I expected. Your name is in it.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: The twig took, dear. I wrapped it myself and it has not even sulked. Tree or farmer, you both settle in fast.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Eight autumns. I told the water spirit I mean to see at least two of them. She did not say no.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: I rang the bell this morning for nobody at all. Just to hear it. Is that allowed? I decided it is.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: How is my little twig doing, dear? Is the stake still holding it straight?

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Water it in the dry weeks, dear. A twig cannot ask you for a drink.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: No fruit yet, but it has decided to grow. Patience is the whole trick, dear.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Don't tug the young branches to see if they've taken root. Leave them be, dear.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Your tree is hung with persimmons! Have you picked any yet, dear? Two a day is plenty.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: The birds found your tree before you did, dear. Let them have the top ones. They know which are sweetest.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: A proper tree now. Keep it watered, dear, and it will pay you back in fall.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Look at those branches. That graft took well, dear. I'm prouder of it than I should be.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Oh, my. You remembered what an old woman likes. Thank you, dear.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: How thoughtful. I'll have it with my afternoon tea.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Thank you, dear.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Ah... my teeth aren't what they were, dear. Give it to Shige.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: A pebble? Are you teasing an old woman?

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: One kindness a day is enough, dear. More and I'll get spoiled.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: A daruma! I'll set it in my alcove and paint an eye for Nana's good health.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Soft and warm, just right for me. Did someone teach you, or are you just kind?

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Home cooking. It's been a while since anyone cooked for me. Thank you.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: A dish for me? Thank you, dear.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Too much for my old jaw, I'm afraid. Nana will enjoy it.
